title: 2 Samuel 18: Deal Gently With the Young Man
body:
Read the chapter → [2 Samuel 18](/bible/2-samuel/18)

**[2 Samuel 18:1-5](/bible/2-samuel/18#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/2-samuel/18#v1)</sup> And David numbered the people that were with him, and set captains of thousands and captains of hundreds over them.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/2-samuel/18#v2)</sup> And David sent forth a third part of the people under the hand of Joab, and a third part under the hand of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, and a third part under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. And the king said unto the people, I will surely go forth with you myself also.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/2-samuel/18#v3)</sup> But the people answered, Thou shalt not go forth: for if we flee away, they will not care for us; neither if half of us die, will they care for us: but now thou art worth ten thousand of us: therefore now it is better that thou succour us out of the city.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/2-samuel/18#v4)</sup> And the king said unto them, What seemeth you best I will do. And the king stood by the gate side, and all the people came out by hundreds and by thousands.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/2-samuel/18#v5)</sup> And the king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Deal gently for my sake with the young man, even with Absalom. And all the people heard when the king gave all the captains charge concerning Absalom.

- David numbered the people and set captains of thousands and hundreds, sending a third part under Joab, a third under Abishai, and a third under Ittai the Gittite. He said he would surely go forth with them himself.
- The people answered that he should not go, for he was worth ten thousand of them and it was better that he support them out of the city. David hearkened to their counsel and said what seemed best to them he would do; he did not run a dictatorship. In a time when he could not trust his own flesh and blood, he trusted the proven men he had warred with for years.
- David charged Joab, Abishai, and Ittai to deal gently for his sake with the young man, even with Absalom, and all the people heard the charge. Even after Absalom defiled his concubines and stole the people's hearts, David still sought to make amends with his son.

**[2 Samuel 18:6-15](/bible/2-samuel/18#v6)**

> <sup>[6](/bible/2-samuel/18#v6)</sup> So the people went out into the field against Israel: and the battle was in the wood of Ephraim;
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/2-samuel/18#v7)</sup> Where the people of Israel were slain before the servants of David, and there was there a great slaughter that day of twenty thousand men.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/2-samuel/18#v8)</sup> For the battle was there scattered over the face of all the country: and the wood devoured more people that day than the sword devoured.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/2-samuel/18#v9)</sup> And Absalom met the servants of David. And Absalom rode upon a mule, and the mule went under the thick boughs of a great oak, and his head caught hold of the oak, and he was taken up between the heaven and the earth; and the mule that was under him went away.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/2-samuel/18#v10)</sup> And a certain man saw it, and told Joab, and said, Behold, I saw Absalom hanged in an oak.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/2-samuel/18#v11)</sup> And Joab said unto the man that told him, And, behold, thou sawest him, and why didst thou not smite him there to the ground? and I would have given thee ten shekels of silver, and a girdle.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/2-samuel/18#v12)</sup> And the man said unto Joab, Though I should receive a thousand shekels of silver in mine hand, yet would I not put forth mine hand against the king’s son: for in our hearing the king charged thee and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Beware that none touch the young man Absalom.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/2-samuel/18#v13)</sup> Otherwise I should have wrought falsehood against mine own life: for there is no matter hid from the king, and thou thyself wouldest have set thyself against me.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/2-samuel/18#v14)</sup> Then said Joab, I may not tarry thus with thee. And he took three darts in his hand, and thrust them through the heart of Absalom, while he was yet alive in the midst of the oak.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/2-samuel/18#v15)</sup> And ten young men that bare Joab’s armour compassed about and smote Absalom, and slew him.

- The battle was in the wood of Ephraim, and Israel was slain before the servants of David in a great slaughter of twenty thousand men. The wood devoured more people that day than the sword devoured.
- Absalom, riding on a mule, went under the thick boughs of a great oak, and his head caught hold of the oak so that he was taken up between the heaven and the earth while the mule went on. He hung there yet alive.
- A man told Joab he had seen Absalom hanged in an oak. Joab asked why he had not smitten him to the ground for a reward of ten shekels and a girdle, but the man refused, saying he would not put forth his hand against the king's son for a thousand shekels, because he had heard the king charge them to beware that none touch the young man.
- The man told Joab that to have killed Absalom would have been to work falsehood against his own life, for nothing is hid from the king, and Joab himself would have set himself against him. Joab said he would not tarry, took three darts, and thrust them through the heart of Absalom while he was yet alive in the midst of the oak.
- Joab was an evil man with the spirit of murder; he could have brought Absalom back alive for his father to make amends, but he did what he wanted. Ten young men that bore Joab's armor compassed Absalom and smote him and slew him, for a beast will consort to his own like.

  Precepts:
  - **[2 Samuel 11:1-7](/bible/2-samuel/11#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/2-samuel/11#v1)</sup> And it came to pass, after the year was expired, at the time when kings go forth to battle, that David sent Joab, and his servants with him, and all Israel; and they destroyed the children of Ammon, and besieged Rabbah. But David tarried still at Jerusalem.
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/2-samuel/11#v2)</sup> And it came to pass in an eveningtide, that David arose from off his bed, and walked upon the roof of the king’s house: and from the roof he saw a woman washing herself; and the woman was very beautiful to look upon.
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/2-samuel/11#v3)</sup> And David sent and enquired after the woman. And one said, Is not this Bath–sheba, the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?
    >
    > <sup>[4](/bible/2-samuel/11#v4)</sup> And David sent messengers, and took her; and she came in unto him, and he lay with her; for she was purified from her uncleanness: and she returned unto her house.
    >
    > <sup>[5](/bible/2-samuel/11#v5)</sup> And the woman conceived, and sent and told David, and said, I am with child.
    >
    > <sup>[6](/bible/2-samuel/11#v6)</sup> And David sent to Joab, saying, Send me Uriah the Hittite. And Joab sent Uriah to David.
    >
    > <sup>[7](/bible/2-samuel/11#v7)</sup> And when Uriah was come unto him, David demanded of him how Joab did, and how the people did, and how the war prospered.

    Joab was David's nephew and the go between in the matter of Bathsheba and the killing of Uriah; Joab knew David's dirt, which is why he often defied the king's orders.

**[2 Samuel 18:16-18](/bible/2-samuel/18#v16)**

> <sup>[16](/bible/2-samuel/18#v16)</sup> And Joab blew the trumpet, and the people returned from pursuing after Israel: for Joab held back the people.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/2-samuel/18#v17)</sup> And they took Absalom, and cast him into a great pit in the wood, and laid a very great heap of stones upon him: and all Israel fled every one to his tent.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/2-samuel/18#v18)</sup> Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken and reared up for himself a pillar, which is in the king’s dale: for he said, I have no son to keep my name in remembrance: and he called the pillar after his own name: and it is called unto this day, Absalom’s place.

- Joab blew the trumpet and held back the people from pursuing Israel. They took Absalom, cast him into a great pit in the woods, and laid a very great heap of stones upon him, and all Israel fled everyone to his tent.
- In his lifetime Absalom had reared up a pillar for himself in the king's dale, saying he had no son to keep his name in remembrance, and he called it after his own name; it is called Absalom's place unto this day.

**[2 Samuel 18:19-33](/bible/2-samuel/18#v19)**

> <sup>[19](/bible/2-samuel/18#v19)</sup> Then said Ahimaaz the son of Zadok, Let me now run, and bear the king tidings, how that the Lord hath avenged him of his enemies.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/2-samuel/18#v20)</sup> And Joab said unto him, Thou shalt not bear tidings this day, but thou shalt bear tidings another day: but this day thou shalt bear no tidings, because the king’s son is dead.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/2-samuel/18#v21)</sup> Then said Joab to Cushi, Go tell the king what thou hast seen. And Cushi bowed himself unto Joab, and ran.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/2-samuel/18#v22)</sup> Then said Ahimaaz the son of Zadok yet again to Joab, But howsoever, let me, I pray thee, also run after Cushi. And Joab said, Wherefore wilt thou run, my son, seeing that thou hast no tidings ready?
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/2-samuel/18#v23)</sup> But howsoever, said he, let me run. And he said unto him, Run. Then Ahimaaz ran by the way of the plain, and overran Cushi.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/2-samuel/18#v24)</sup> And David sat between the two gates: and the watchman went up to the roof over the gate unto the wall, and lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold a man running alone.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/2-samuel/18#v25)</sup> And the watchman cried, and told the king. And the king said, If he be alone, there is tidings in his mouth. And he came apace, and drew near.
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/2-samuel/18#v26)</sup> And the watchman saw another man running: and the watchman called unto the porter, and said, Behold another man running alone. And the king said, He also bringeth tidings.
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/2-samuel/18#v27)</sup> And the watchman said, Me thinketh the running of the foremost is like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok. And the king said, He is a good man, and cometh with good tidings.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/2-samuel/18#v28)</sup> And Ahimaaz called, and said unto the king, All is well. And he fell down to the earth upon his face before the king, and said, Blessed be the Lord thy God, which hath delivered up the men that lifted up their hand against my lord the king.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/2-samuel/18#v29)</sup> And the king said, Is the young man Absalom safe? And Ahimaaz answered, When Joab sent the king’s servant, and me thy servant, I saw a great tumult, but I knew not what it was.
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/2-samuel/18#v30)</sup> And the king said unto him, Turn aside, and stand here. And he turned aside, and stood still.
>
> <sup>[31](/bible/2-samuel/18#v31)</sup> And, behold, Cushi came; and Cushi said, Tidings, my lord the king: for the Lord hath avenged thee this day of all them that rose up against thee.
>
> <sup>[32](/bible/2-samuel/18#v32)</sup> And the king said unto Cushi, Is the young man Absalom safe? And Cushi answered, The enemies of my lord the king, and all that rise against thee to do thee hurt, be as that young man is.
>
> <sup>[33](/bible/2-samuel/18#v33)</sup> And the king was much moved, and went up to the chamber over the gate, and wept: and as he went, thus he said, O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! would God I had died for thee, O Absalom, my son, my son!

- Ahimaaz wanted to run and bear the king the tidings that the Lord had avenged him of his enemies, but Joab first sent Cushi, since the king's son was dead and this was not good news to carry. Ahimaaz pressed again and was allowed to run, and he outran Cushi by way of the plain.
- David sat between the two gates while the watchman on the wall saw first Ahimaaz running alone, then another man. The king said a man running alone brings tidings, and he recognized the running of Ahimaaz as a good man coming with good news.
- Ahimaaz fell before the king and said all was well, blessing the Lord who had delivered up the men that lifted their hand against the king; the good news was that David was alive and had overcome. When David asked if the young man Absalom was safe, Ahimaaz said he saw a great tumult but knew not what it was.
- Cushi came and said the enemies of the king and all that rose against him should be as that young man is. David understood that his son was one of the casualties of war. He was much moved, went up to the chamber over the gate, and wept, crying, O my son Absalom, would God I had died for thee. David's whole life was war, slaughtering giants from his youth up, and now he mourned in heartache for his son.
